issue.title: fix(upf): delete old PFCP sessions on a new association setup

repository.name: oai-cn5g-upf
repository.description: OAI 5G Core Network User Plane Function (UPF)

issue.body:
Closes #41

### Problem

When a CP function that is already associated sends a PFCP Association Setup Request again, the UPF overwrites the association but keeps the PFCP sessions of the old one. TS 29.244 clause 6.2.6.2.2 requires the UP function to delete them unless PFCP Session Retention Information asks to keep them. The UPF does not decode that IE.

After an SMF restart this breaks new sessions. The SMF allocates CP SEIDs from 1 again. A request whose CP F-SEID equals that of a kept session is rejected, and the UE gets a PDU Session Establishment Reject (#38). Details and logs are in #41.

### Change

Two commits:

1. `pfcp_association::del_sessions()` no longer holds `m_sessions` while it removes the sessions. With usage reporting on (simple switch), `pfcp_switch::remove_pfcp_session()` sends a final usage report for a session with traffic since its last report. To send it, `upf_n4::send_n4_msg()` calls `pfcp_associations::get_association(cp_fseid)`, which locks `m_sessions` again in `has_session()`, on the same thread. The sessions are now moved out of the set under the lock and removed after it is released. Their final reports then find no association and are not sent. After commit 2, the heartbeat failure path is the only caller of `del_sessions()`, and this commit fixes the same deadlock there.
2. `upf_n4::handle_receive_association_setup_request()` looks up the existing association for the Node ID. If there is one, it takes the association's session set (`pfcp_association::take_sessions()`) before `add_association()` overwrites it, and sends it to `TASK_UPF_APP` in a new ITTI message, `itti_n4_association_sessions_deletion`. `upf_app` then calls `pfcp_switch::remove_pfcp_session()` for each session. A first association is not affected.

   The Setup Request is handled on the N4 receive thread, but `pfcp_switch` changes `cp_fseid2pfcp_sessions` and the session objects only on `TASK_UPF_APP` (`pfcp_switch.hpp`: "all modifications must be serialised"). Deleting there keeps that rule. The ITTI queue is FIFO, and the message is queued before the Setup Response is sent, so `TASK_UPF_APP` deletes the old sessions before it handles any session request of the new association.

### Testing

**First revision (sessions deleted on the N4 receive thread; changed after review, see below), arm64.** Live, on an OAI RF simulator testbed: OAI gNB and 4 nrUEs, AMF and SMF v2.2.2 with local patches for stale UE contexts and stale PDU sessions (none changes PFCP association handling or SEID allocation), and UPF with the simple switch. The changed files are the same on `develop` and `v2.2.2`, so the commits were applied to `v2.2.2` for the test. Each run: `docker restart oai-smf`, then restart one UE.

- **Official `oai-upf:v2.2.2`:** the UPF kept the 4 old sessions. The UPF rejected the new N4 Session Establishment Request with CP SEID 0x1, and the SMF sent PDU Session Establishment Reject #38 to the UE.
- **Both commits, usage reporting off:** the UPF logs `PFCP association with 192.168.71.133 already exists, deleting its PFCP sessions`. The new session with CP SEID 0x1 is accepted, the UPF has only that session, and the UE pings the DN.
- **First-revision commit 2 only (calling `del_sessions()` on the N4 thread), usage reporting on, UEs sending traffic:** after the deletion log the UPF never sent the Association Setup Response. The SMF kept logging `Failed to receive PFCP Association Response, Retrying`, the old sessions stayed, and the UE got no session.
- **Both commits, usage reporting on, UEs sending traffic:** the UPF logs `Could not send PFCP_SESSION_REPORT_REQUEST, cause association not found for cp_fseid` once per old session, answers the Setup, accepts the new session with CP SEID 0x1, and the UE pings the DN.
- **First association after a UPF start:** no deletion log, and 4 UEs attach and ping as before.
- **Build:** `develop` with both commits builds (`docker/Dockerfile.upf.ubuntu`, target `oai-upf`, arm64) with no warning in the changed files. clang-format 19.1.1 gives no change.

**Current revision (sessions deleted on `TASK_UPF_APP`), x86_64, same kind of testbed with the official `v2.2.2` AMF and SMF, usage reporting on and 3 UEs pinging the DN during the SMF restart:**

- The UPF logs `PFCP association with 172.29.71.133 already exists, deleting its PFCP sessions` (N4), then `Associated with CP function`, then `Deleting 4 PFCP sessions of a replaced association` (`upf_app`). The new session with CP SEID 0x1 is registered after that, and the UE pings the DN. Same result with a ThreadSanitizer build; it reports no race in the new code.
- We could not show the race on `cp_fseid2pfcp_sessions` itself with ThreadSanitizer: after an SMF restart, no session request arrives until the Setup Response is sent, so the two threads never use the map at the same time. The case where they can is a Setup Request from a CP function that has not restarted (see Notes).
- `develop` with both commits builds with no warning in the changed files (x86_64). clang-format 19 gives no change.

In one of the two runs with both commits and usage reporting on, the UPF stopped with SIGSEGV about 90 s after its first association, before the SMF restart. No session deletion had run at that point: the first Setup found no existing association, and heartbeats were answered until the crash. We kept only the end of that log. The official image with usage reporting on ran 5 min without a crash. On x86_64, a build of this branch without ThreadSanitizer stopped once the same way, about 50 s after start and before any re-association: its last lines are a heartbeat request received from the SMF and a heartbeat request sent by the UPF in the same millisecond. This matches the data races in the PFCP stack reported in #44 (fix in #45), not the code of this PR.

### Notes

- The heartbeat failure path (`timeout_heartbeat_request()` on `TASK_UPF_N4`) still deletes sessions outside `TASK_UPF_APP`, as before this PR. It could use the same message; that is not changed here.
- The final usage report of a deleted session is not sent: its association look-up by CP F-SEID finds nothing once the set has been taken. After an SMF restart the SMF does not know these sessions anyway. For a Setup Request from a CP function that has not restarted, the report is lost; TS 29.244 does not require it for this case.
- The order of the deletion and the new session requests relies on the SMF not sending a session request before it receives the Setup Response (TS 29.244 §6.2.6.2.1). The UPF does not check this. A session request sent earlier can find an old session with the same CP F-SEID and is rejected with `Request rejected`; a later attempt is accepted.
- The OAI SMF also sends an Association Setup Request to an already associated UPF when the NRF notifies it that the UPF registered (`process_upf_profile()` → `itti_n4_association_retry`). With this change, the UPF then deletes the sessions, as TS 29.244 requires. If that SMF behaviour should change, that is for the SMF repository.
